reviewNotes: The first full run includes the actual sponsor mission. Its working-tree production-build phase was mistakenly labeled clean_source; only the distinct independent install/build/sample phases used the clean export. The final offline run corrects that label and adds a start/end source-hash check. Original first-run bytes/timings/results are preserved unchanged.
No sponsor calls were repeated for report-only/source-review fixes. Application src/ and live verifier behavior were unchanged between these two runs.

An initial source-review check reported two credential-bearing URL findings; review identified an environment-variable placeholder and the existing deliberately invalid password fixture. Template and narrowly scoped fixture handling was corrected; final tracked/untracked scans passed. Findings were never real exposed keys.

Named tests cover controlled TLS/rate/auth/timeout faults, not real fault injection against sponsor services. Prior actual source-mutation/restoration evidence and earlier mobile/Stop waiting browser observations are referenced as historical, not recaptured.
limits: One actual sponsor planning run is a functional check, not a reliability estimate. Mock/scenario times are not averaged with sponsor time.

Measured sample generator invocations are logical calls to deterministic substitutes; they are not hosted model calls. Overall regression generator totals are uninstrumented. Runtime internal provider fan-out is not counted by Relay HTTP metrics.

Live planning used actual Nightshift/Zetaris transports and synthetic campus business data, with two Runtime-reported NVIDIA Nemotron models correlated to persisted receipts. Exact Lightning pinning, cryptographic verification and independent NVIDIA attestation remain unverified.
A21-A23 are untested/deferred. No real provider booking, inventory reservation/purchase, payment, private ROVER implementation, deployment or publication occurred.
